1:# Editor Scope
3:## How To Build
7:## Theme
11:## Concept
13:### Pitch
17:### Shape
19:#### Description
23:#### Layout
28:#### Syntax Highlighting
33:#### Selecting Text
44:#### Ruler
48:#### Wrap
52:#### Keyboard
54:##### Indentation
58:##### Backspace
62:##### Home
66:##### New Lines
70:###### Instead
76:#### New Files
80:#### Saving
#### Layout

Everything in the tab is laid out the same plain way, with no stray padding or margin anywhere. The header runs the tab's full width, 32 pixels tall, as tall as the body's tab bar, its contents centred up and down in it, with 12 pixels of padding at its left and 8 at its right, and a single 1 pixel line in the theme's line colour along its bottom, the only line in the tab. In it, from the left: the file's path, then 6 pixels after it the unsaved dot while there is one, then at the far right the Wrap button, the Save button, and the close button, 4 pixels apart. All are small ghost buttons 24 pixels tall, the Wrap and close buttons icon buttons 24 pixels square, none with a border. The header has no margin of its own above, below, or beside it: it starts at the top of the tab, directly beneath the tab bar, and its left and right edges are the tab's.
Beneath the header, the file fills the rest of the tab edge to edge, with no margin, border, or rounded corner around it, and nothing between it and the header's line. Its text starts 12 pixels in from the tab's left edge, the same as the path in the header above it, so the two line up, and 8 pixels below the header's line. A message that the file can't be read, or can't be saved, is set in by the same 12 pixels, in a row as tall as its text needs with 8 pixels above and below it.

#### Wrap

The Wrap button, with a wrap-text icon, turns soft wrapping on and off, showing as selected while it is on. Its tooltip says whether long lines wrap or run past the edge, and that clicking does the other, with its shortcut, Alt+Z. It starts off. While it is on, a line longer than the editor is wide wraps at the editor's right edge, at a space where there is one and mid-word where there isn't, onto as many visual rows as it needs, each row after the first starting at the line's own indentation, so the text never scrolls sideways and the horizontal scrollbar goes. Only how the text shows changes: the file's text, its line numbers, the language server's positions, and what is saved are the same either way, and Home, End, and selecting by line act on visual rows while on, as in other editors, Home's smart indentation applying to the line's first row. The ruler and its shade stay at the 80th column, wrapped or not. Turning it on or off keeps the cursor's line in view where it was. The choice is remembered for the user, as the [UserPreferencesScope](../user-preferences/index.md#user-preferences-scope) says, the same for every file and project, and holds for every file opened after.

 - the interface's brightness, one for dark mode and one for light, each starting at 0 - the colours chosen in the theme editor, the base and Code, Chain, Spec, and Ask, for dark mode and for light, each the theme's own until chosen; restored before brightness, which they bound - whether the editor wraps long lines, as the [EditorScope](../editor/index.md#editor-scope) says, off until turned on - whether the ribbon is collapsed, which starts expanded - the layout of a file's diff, which starts side by side - the recent projects - the folder a project was last opened from - the harness runs go 
--

The editor header now has a Wrap button, with a wrap-text icon just before Save, and Alt+Z does the same. On the full run 555 tests passed and `referenced_spec_shows_the_understanding` failed; it's been flaky before and passed three times on its own. I haven't tried it in the running app.

- **The button:** shows as selected while wrapping is on. Its tooltip says what long lines do now, what clicking does, and gives the shortcut.
- **What wrapping does:** long lines wrap at the editor's edge, at a space where there is one, and each wrapped row keeps the line's indentation. There is no sideways scrolling while it's on. The file's text, line numbers and saving don't change.
- **Remembered:** the choice is saved and applies to every open file and every file opened later. It starts off.
- **Home:** on a wrapped row after a line's first, Home goes to that row's start; the existing smart indentation only applies on the first row.
- **Cursor stays put:** toggling keeps the cursor's line where it was on screen.

The spec and your prompt agree. A new test covers the button, Alt+Z, and the line actually wrapping; the Home behaviour has no test.
